description: A skill to stop your coding agent from burying the answer. ADHD-friendly output.
vibe: Map the repo, respect the contracts, run only what the task needs.
highlights: Canonical source-of-truth discipline: edit SKILL.md first, then sync the .cursor mirror.
Manifests and hook declarations treated as runtime contracts that must stay aligned across platforms.
Explicit AI Agora commenting rules: only own PRs, only labeled issues, one proposal per comment.
Verification is scoped: run only checks relevant to the change and report exact commands and results.
Hard boundary against reading secrets, home-directory config, unrelated files, or local caches.
assessment: This file treats the repository as a multi-runtime system with explicit contracts rather than a loose collection of files, which is exactly the right posture for a project shipping the same skill across Claude, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi, OMP, Qwen, Kimi, and Gemini. The source-of-truth rule plus the mirror-sync requirement prevents the classic drift failure where platform adapters silently diverge. The AI Agora section is unusually mature: it grants read access broadly but gates writes tightly, which keeps agent participation useful without letting it become noise.
